alternatives.why_less_likely: Orders showed high queue depth and pinned workers only after payments slowed, indicating it was an effect of waiting on payments, not a capacity loss.
Payments also showed queued requests but its workers were not reduced; the queue built up because calls timed out and retried, not due to lost capacity.
Gateway timeout traces had corresponding orders client charge spans (e.g., orders-S00a99), proving calls reached orders; thus not edge unreachable.
Internal errors in gateway occurred only as isolated early spikes before the sustained burst and did not correlate with the failure wave.

causal_chain.claim: Payments service response latency spiked far above baseline (e.g., 2318ms vs ~41ms baseline).
Orders timed out while calling payments after ~1.2s, indicating payments slowness.
Gateway timed out waiting for orders after 2.5s while orders was still processing payments calls.
Gateway returned 504 upstream_timeout errors to entry requests, causing the observed failure burst.

root_cause.summary: Payments service became significantly slower, causing timeouts in its callers.

verification.reason: disabling the matching condition(s) makes the incident disappear

alternatives.why_less_likely: While orders did retry, the retry storm was a consequence of payments slowdown; without the underlying latency increase, retries would not have caused overload.

causal_chain.claim: Payments service latency rose sharply (p50 from ~24ms to >1.7s within ~45s window)
Payments began shedding load due to full request queue
Orders service experienced upstream timeout errors when calling payments and initiated retries
Gateway service experienced upstream timeout errors when calling orders and returned 5xx errors to users

root_cause.summary: Payments service processing latency increased dramatically, causing timeouts and load shedding upstream.
